item.title: Paytm sees 10x rise in net profit in Q2 of FY27
item.description: The company's revenue for the second quarter of FY27 stood at Rs 2,648 crore, which was an annual growth of 28.4%.
item.content:encoded:
Paytm reported a net profit of Rs 225 crore for the second quarter of FY27, which was almost a 10x rise when compared to Rs 21 crore recorded in the similar period of last fiscal.

The revenue for the second quarter came in at Rs 2,648 crore as compared to Rs 2,061 crore registered in the similar period of last fiscal, recording a year-on-year (YoY) growth of 28.4%.

According to the company, the EBITDA rose 90% on a year-on-year basis with the EBITDA margin expanding to 10%. Paytm said distribution of financial services revenue grew 49% YoY to Rs 912 crore, with key financial services customers increasing 35% YoY to 8.8 lakh. The net payment revenue increased 21% YoY on a comparable basis to Rs 644 crore.

According to Paytm, with a focus on monetisable user base, it gained consumer UPI payment market share for the sixth consecutive quarter, with Paytm UPI GTV growing at more than double the industry growth rate. Monthly transacting users increased by 1 crore YoY to 8.5 crore, the highest addition in nearly three years, driven by better product, stronger acquisition and retention, and AI-led personalisation.

Paytm said AI is increasingly becoming the operating system with fine-tuned models and agents deployed across consumer, merchant and engineering journeys, risk management, collections, fraud prevention and personalisation. AI-led efficiencies helped reduce indirect expenses as a share of revenue to 46% from 52% a year ago. The company has also begun offering its AI platform to enterprise merchants, extending its in-house capabilities to help them grow and engage customers across channels.

Paytm said with a large addressable market, accelerating revenue growth and AI-led improvements in structural operating leverage, it expects sustained revenue growth and margin expansion to drive long-term profit growth.

item.title: Startup news and updates: Daily roundup (October 27, 2026)
item.description: YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Tuesday, October 27, 2026.
item.content:encoded:
YourStory brings you today's headlines and the latest news across sectors.

Featured stories 

Naiyya Saggi on building EDT

Naiyya Saggi, founder of consumer appliance and beauty-tech startup EDT (Everyday Design & Technology), is reimagining everyday products for Indian consumers. Founded in 2025 with co-founder Vyasateja Rao, the startup offers a range of devices for the home, kitchen and beauty segments. Its products include Luma, a programmable glass air fryer; Flow, a temperature-controlled glass kettle; and SUKI, a hair dryer designed to minimise hair damage.

Saggi, who previously founded parenting platform BabyChakra and co-founded the Good Glamm Group, says EDT aims to address market gaps by combining thoughtful design with technology tailored to Indian consumers.

Read more

Sarvam AI signs five-year agreement with Defence Ministry to develop AI technology

Indian AI startup Sarvam AI has signed a five-year agreement with the Ministry of Defence to develop artificial intelligence (AI) technology for the armed forces. The partnership aims to strengthen India's indigenous AI capabilities for defence applications and reduce dependence on foreign technology for sensitive military operations.

Founded by Pratyush Kumar and Vivek Raghavan, Sarvam AI develops AI models and tools tailored to Indian languages and contexts. Its defence work comes amid the government's push to build homegrown AI systems for military applications, including intelligence analysis, surveillance, reconnaissance, and operational decision-making. The collaboration could help integrate indigenous AI capabilities into India's defence ecosystem.

Read more

Funding news

Live2.ai raises Rs 130 Cr to expand AI-led social commerce platform

Bengaluru-based Live2.ai, which uses artificial intelligence (AI) to connect social media intelligence with marketing and commerce, has raised Rs 130 crore ($14 million) in a pre-Series B funding round led by venture capital firm IvyCap Ventures. The round includes fresh capital to fund expansion and a secondary component that gives early shareholders partial liquidity.

Founded by J Venkat and Neha Suyal, Live2.ai helps brands monitor conversations across social media platforms, analyse trends, audit influencer content, publish campaigns and measure performance.

Read more

Maasi raises Rs 6 Cr to build a reliable nanny service for Indian parents

Bengaluru-based childcare startup Maasi has raised Rs 6 crore in a pre-seed funding round led by Better Capital, alongside Antler India. Angel investors, including Rapido veteran Rishikesh SR, Shadowfax’s Vaibhav Khandelwal, Xoxoday’s Sumit Khandelwal, Siddhant Goyal, and Sanjay Ramakrishnan, also participated. Following its public launch on October 20, the startup says it attracted a waitlist of more than 4,000 parents within five days and has served over 1,200 parents through a network of more than 500 caregivers.

Founded by Aashu Manchali, Gargi Pandey, and Reshov Roy, Maasi aims to solve the challenge of finding reliable childcare by offering verified, trained nannies.

Mochatrade raises $5.5M to expand US markets trading platform for Indian users

Mochatrade has raised $5.5 million in total funding for its US markets trading platform targeting Indian users. The funding was led by CoinFund, with participation from Coinbase Ventures, Zero Knowledge Ventures and other investors. Earlier backers include Y Combinator and Pioneer Fund. The platform aims to make trading linked to US-listed companies such as Nvidia and Tesla more accessible to Indian users.

Mochatrade lets users fund accounts through UPI and track margins, profits, and losses in rupees. Its platform offers long and short positions through perpetual futures contracts linked to US company prices, without requiring users to open a US brokerage account or own the underlying shares. These contracts have no fixed expiry, and leverage lets traders take larger positions with less upfront capital, increasing both potential gains and losses.

CopperPilot raises $390K to build AI design agent for electronics hardware

CopperPilot, an AI-powered design agent for electronics hardware, has raised $390,000 in a pre-seed funding round led by Neon Fund, with participation from US-based angel investors. The startup also announced the release of the first version of its design agent, codenamed Epsilon, which is now available to hardware engineers. CopperPilot says its weekly active users have grown 25-fold since August 2026, and it has run more than 6,000 design tasks, or artefacts, on the platform to date.

The startup aims to simplify electronic circuit board design by automating tasks such as reading component datasheets, selecting parts, drawing schematics and routing circuit boards. These processes can take engineers several weeks and cost thousands of dollars before they have a first prototype. CopperPilot aims to reduce this timeline to hours, helping hardware teams accelerate product development and reduce engineering workloads.

dubdub raises $1.3M seed round led by 3one4 Capital, others

dubdub, a swipe-based trivia and puzzle app, has raised $1.3 million in a seed funding round led by 3one4 Capital, Antler and Stellaris Venture Partners. Founded by second-time entrepreneurs Kaustubh Priye and Supan Shah, who previously built and sold health-tech company Aldun to Care.Fi, the startup plans to use the funds to expand its product and engineering teams, introduce new interactive formats and improve personalisation.

Launched in March 2026, dubdub has crossed 20,000 downloads. The app aims to replace passive scrolling with interactive content, including questions, puzzles and mini-games across more than 20 categories, such as cricket, Bollywood, pop culture, mythology, general knowledge and logical reasoning. It uses AI and user interactions to personalise challenges, while letting users compete with friends, compare scores, and share their experiences.

Nova Spectral AI Raises Rs 21.15 Cr in seed round

Bengaluru-based deeptech startup Nova Spectral AI has raised Rs 21.15 crore in a seed funding round led by Shastra VC, with participation from Equirus InnovateX Fund and angel investors. The company is developing a quantum dot-based short-wave infrared (SWIR) image sensor chip designed for drones, surveillance systems, robots, autonomous vehicles and other physical AI applications. Its technology uses indium arsenide quantum dots and CMOS-compatible manufacturing processes to target sensor costs up to 100 times lower than conventional indium gallium arsenide technology.

The startup aims to reduce India's dependence on imported infrared sensors while making advanced imaging more affordable. Co-founder and CEO Anish Priyadarshi said the funding would support team expansion and development of a field-ready prototype within 18 months.

Tensrai Secures investment from Finvolve and India Accelerator

Hyderabad-based Physical AI startup Tensrai has secured an undisclosed investment from venture capital fund Finvolve and India Accelerator. The company will deploy the capital towards technology development, engineering, customer deployments and market expansion. Founded in 2022, Tensrai is developing a unified autonomy platform that enables industrial and commercial robots and vehicles to perceive, navigate, learn and perform physical tasks. Its technology combines AI-based localisation, intelligent navigation and mission planning, including operations in GPS-denied environments.

The startup is also developing capabilities that allow robots to learn tasks through human demonstrations. Its applications include material movement, cleaning and robotic manipulation across factories, warehouses, hospitals and commercial campuses. Tensrai's business model includes robot sales, retrofitting, Robot-as-a-Service and customised solutions.

Other news

Aleph appoints Medhavi Singh as India Country Head

Global digital advertising and fintech solutions company Aleph has appointed Medhavi Singh as its Country Head for India. The appointment reflects the company's focus on India's digital economy and the country's growing importance in the Asia-Pacific region.

Singh brings over 15 years of experience across digital advertising, retail media, quick commerce and revenue strategy.

She joins Aleph after nearly nine years at Criteo, where she most recently served as Country Head for India and helped grow the company's business in the market.

Before Criteo, she spent nearly five years at Google in account strategy and analytical leadership roles across India, the UK, and the US.

She holds a degree in computer science engineering and an MBA.


Protectt.ai acquires majority stake in Bosch-incubated AIShield

Cybersecurity company Protectt.ai Labs has made a strategic investment in AIShield, an AI security platform incubated within Bosch Global Software Technologies (BGSW), becoming its majority shareholder. The investment comprises a primary share issuance and a secondary purchase from existing investors. Following the transaction, AIShield will operate as an independent entity, AI Shield Private Limited (AISW), under Protectt.ai.

The capital will support AIShield's research and development, international expansion and development of sovereign AI security capabilities as organisations increasingly seek to secure AI systems against emerging cyber threats.

Skydo gets IFSCA authorisation to expand cross-border payment services

Cross-border payments platform Skydo has received final authorisation from the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA) to operate as a Payment Service Provider (PSP) at Gujarat International Finance Tec-City (GIFT City) International Financial Services Centre (IFSC). The approval follows the in-principle authorisation granted in May 2026 and enables the company to develop a broader range of cross-border payment products.

Skydo plans to introduce multi-currency accounts, merchant acquiring and collections, and payment infrastructure for exporters, investment platforms and trade finance companies operating in the IFSC. One proposed offering is a multi-currency account that will allow eligible Indian exporters to collect and hold foreign currency, use it to pay overseas suppliers, or convert it into rupees when required, subject to regulatory requirements.

TagMango partners with ClickFunnels to launch Backstage Pass for creators

TagMango, a Y Combinator-backed creator monetisation platform, has launched Backstage Pass in partnership with ClickFunnels, a sales-funnel platform whose users have generated over $11 billion in sales.

TagMango works with more than 10,000 creators and has reached over 15 million users, while ClickFunnels has a community of more than 150,000 customers. Unveiled at Funnel Hacking Live in Las Vegas, Backstage Pass will initially target the US market before expanding to India.

The platform aims to help creators engage and monetise their audiences directly, without relying on social media algorithms for visibility.

Mudrex report maps India's real-world asset tokenisation landscape

Crypto investment platform Mudrex has released The Builder’s Guide to RWA Tokenization in India, a report examining the state of real-world asset (RWA) tokenisation across seven asset classes: commodities, currencies, bonds, equities, real estate and land, credit, and energy. The report finds that India has established much of the public infrastructure required for tokenisation, with the next phase of growth depending on businesses developing solutions using these existing systems.

According to the report, bonds and energy have seen government-led pilots, while Maharashtra has committed to introducing a land-tokenisation law. In credit, market participants have explored blockchain-based warehouse-receipt lending and invoice tokenisation through the Reserve Bank of India's sandbox. However, commodities, currencies and equities remain largely untapped opportunities.

The report highlights the potential for innovations such as blockchain-based gold tokens backed by physical gold, cross-border central bank digital currency (CBDC) transactions and regulated tokenisation of listed shares.

Amazon to deploy 3,000 Tata electric trucks across India

Amazon and Tata Motors have announced a collaboration to deploy 3,000 electric trucks across Amazon's transportation network in India. The deployment, described as the largest electric-truck rollout by an e-commerce company in the country, will extend Amazon's fleet electrification efforts beyond last-mile delivery. The trucks will transport customer shipments between facilities, across cities and along national freight corridors. The first batch of vehicles was flagged off in Delhi in the presence of Union Minister for Heavy Industries and Steel HD Kumaraswamy and senior executives from both companies.

Under the arrangement, Tata Motors will supply the electric trucks, while Amazon's carrier partners will own and operate them. The initiative combines Amazon's logistics network and freight demand with Tata Motors' vehicle manufacturing, engineering and servicing capabilities. The companies aim to accelerate the adoption of electric freight transportation in India and demonstrate the potential of zero-tailpipe-emission trucks for large-scale logistics operations.

BikeWo Green Tech partners with Green Drive Mobility to scale electric logistics

BikeWo Green Tech Limited has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Green Drive Auto Services, also known as Green Drive Mobility, to jointly develop and expand electric logistics operations across India. The partnership will focus on last-mile, mid-mile and long-haul freight transportation, with the companies aiming to build a green logistics platform with a fleet of at least 5,000 electric trucks over the coming years.

Green Drive Mobility currently operates more than 350 electric trucks and approximately 8,000 electric two-wheelers. Its truck logistics clients include More Retail, DHL and Gati. The company also provides ONDC-enabled last-mile logistics services, supporting quick-commerce businesses through its electric two-wheeler fleet. The collaboration aims to expand electric-vehicle use across India's freight and logistics sector.

US wealth management firm AssetMark opens Hyderabad GCC

US-based wealth management platform AssetMark has opened a Global Capability Centre (GCC) in Hyderabad, with capacity to accommodate approximately 500 employees. The centre will strengthen the company's global technology and business operations while expanding its presence in India. AssetMark has operated in the country through an outsourcing model for nearly a decade. The new facility will bring dedicated operations and technology teams in-house to support its wealth management platform, including artificial intelligence initiatives. Led locally by Joshi Alaparthi, Vice President and Head of India GCC, the team will collaborate with US-based colleagues on engineering, operations and product management. Hiring is underway across experience levels, with the company planning to recruit 10–15 graduates from Chaitanya Bharathi Institute of Technology as its first campus recruitment cohort.

Bounteous expands Bengaluru office to strengthen enterprise AI capabilities

AI services firm Bounteous has inaugurated an expanded office in Bengaluru as it scales its enterprise AI capabilities and global delivery operations. The facility will provide additional workspace for collaboration among engineering, data and technology transformation teams serving clients worldwide. Bounteous has operated in India for more than two decades and serves over 70 Fortune Global 2000 clients. In June 2026, the company joined Anthropic's Claude Partner Network as a launch Preferred Services Partner. Since then, it has built a team of more than 1,000 certified Claude architects to help enterprises integrate AI into their workflows. Its proprietary Bounteous Arc platform supports the design, development and deployment of AI agents. The company has more than 5,000 employees globally, with operations in Bengaluru, Chennai, Gurugram, and Hyderabad.

IIM Calcutta Innovation Park, AIM train incubation professionals

IIM Calcutta Innovation Park (IIMCIP) and Atal Innovation Mission (AIM), under NITI Aayog, have conducted a three-day residential capacity-building programme for 20 incubation and innovation professionals from institutions across India. Held at the IIM Calcutta campus, the AIM-AiPEX programme aims to strengthen the capabilities of professionals supporting startups and entrepreneurship.

The initiative addresses the growing need for skilled incubation managers as India's ecosystem expands to more than 1,200 incubation centres. Participants received practical training in startup sourcing and selection, programme design, enterprise support, go-to-market strategies, fund management, legal compliance, governance and performance monitoring.

The programme included expert-led sessions, practical exercises and interactions with mentors and entrepreneurs. IIMCIP said the initiative would help participants apply their learnings to strengthen startup support in their respective institutions.

The Func. Lab launches creatine-based hydration and protein products

Indian functional nutrition brand The Func. Lab has introduced two creatine-based product lines, CREASalts and Crea Protein, designed to integrate supplementation into everyday hydration and protein routines. CREASalts combines 3g of creatine monohydrate with electrolytes and taurine per serving. It is available in four flavours, with prices starting at Rs 500 for 15 servings.

The protein range combines 3g of creatine with either plant-based protein or whey protein and comes in multiple flavours. Plant Protein + Creatine is priced from Rs 600 for a travel pack, while Whey Protein + Creatine starts at Rs 1,500. The company said the products aim to simplify daily supplementation by combining commonly used nutrition products. Founded by Sohrab Khushrushahi, Sahil Kukreja and Daneesh Davar, the brand targets consumers seeking performance and functional nutrition solutions.

GetCompanion expands in-person companionship services to Delhi

GetCompanion, a human presence platform, has expanded its in-person companionship services from Gurugram to Delhi. The startup connects users with trained, verified companions for conversation, shared interests, and everyday activities, including walks, shopping, restaurant visits, games, and hospital visits. The company clarified that its services do not include therapy, medical advice, caregiving or physical assistance.

Founder and CEO Shradha Chaturvedi said the expansion aims to make human connection more accessible to people living away from family, adjusting to new cities or seeking company during personal transitions. To ensure safety, meetings are restricted to verified residences or secure public locations, such as parks, malls and cafes. Companions undergo identity and background checks, police verification, psychometric assessments and specialised training. GetCompanion plans to expand into additional Indian cities.

COTRAV BLACK enters premium live entertainment market

COTRAV BLACK, an ultra-premium live-experiences platform, has announced its entry into India's luxury entertainment market. The brand will offer invite-only VIP enclosures at concerts, sporting events and cultural occasions, targeting business leaders, entrepreneurs and high-net-worth individuals. Its debut is scheduled for A.R. Rahman's concert at Mumbai's Jio World Centre on November 1, 2026.

The experience will include curated guest lists, private viewing areas, personalised hospitality and premium food and beverage services. The initiative comes amid growth in India's organised live-events industry, which expanded 44% to Rs 14,500 crore in 2025 and is projected to reach Rs 19,600 crore by 2028. Backed by the group behind travel management company COTRAV, the platform also envisages selective partnerships with brands and financial institutions.

Powerplay reports up to fourfold growth in platform spending after AI Adoption

Construction technology platform Powerplay has reported up to fourfold growth in platform spending over approximately 18 months among customers adopting its AI agents. The Bengaluru-based company offers an AI Purchase Executive to help contractors compare supplier prices, track material requirements and check purchase orders against budgets. Its AI Credit Analyst helps organise project information and financing documents for loan applications through lending partners. Powerplay said its annualised marketplace transaction volume increased from approximately Rs 36 crore to around Rs 100 crore over the past year.

Financing volume facilitated through lending partners grew more than eightfold from a small base, across four cities. The platform represents more than 40,000 construction firms and 85,000 projects. Founded by Iesh Dixit and Shubham Goyal, Powerplay is expanding its AI-led procurement and financing capabilities.

Digi Yatra begins international passenger trials across seven Indian airports

Digi Yatra has commenced trials to extend its digital identity platform to international air travel at seven Indian airports: Delhi, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Kochi, Mumbai, Chennai and Amritsar.

Running from October to December 2026, the three-month trial will allow Indian nationals holding e-passports and travelling on Air India and IndiGo international flights to use Digi Yatra at designated airport touchpoints, including terminal entry, security areas, and boarding gates, subject to infrastructure availability. The trials cover all international destinations served by Air India and select destinations served by IndiGo.

Eligible passengers can create an e-passport-based Verifiable Credential through the Digi Yatra app by scanning their passport’s Machine Readable Zone, reading its embedded chip using a compatible smartphone’s NFC capability, and completing a selfie-based verification process. The passenger's device stores the credential in their Digi Yatra wallet, where they can use it at enabled touchpoints during the trial.

Passengers must continue to carry their travel documents and complete mandatory airline document checks, immigration and other travel formalities. Trial feedback is expected to inform plans for a wider rollout in 2027.

item.title: Capital no longer creates jobs, and AI is compounding the issue: Yatish Rajawat of Hundred Million Jobs
item.description: At TechSparks 2026, K Yatish Rajawat of Hundred Million Jobs said MSMEs, data laws, entrepreneurship and reskilling will shape the next wave of employment in the country.
item.content:encoded:
India's growth model is quietly severing the link between investment and employment, said K Yatish Rajawat, Co-founder of Hundred Million Jobs, a non-profit initiative to create 100 million net jobs in India over the next decade.

Capital is no longer creating jobs at scale, he said, at TechSparks, YourStory's flagship tech-startup summit.

The employment problem is different across cities, be it Delhi, Mumbai or Bengaluru, he observed. In Bengaluru, for instance, the debate is often around AI and its impact on jobs.

The damage began roughly a decade ago on the factory floors, driven by automation, he opined. Even a firm with a turnover of Rs 10 crore or Rs 50 crore now has robots, he said, and the machines are constantly evolving and getting better. They no longer simply move a widget from one point to another. They respond to their surroundings, and handle a range of materials, including cloth and paper, not just sheet metal, said Rajawat.

Even labour-intensive work such as welding and forging has been impacted due to automation, he said. He expects services to follow suit.

Referring to a book by Nobel Prize winners and MIT professors, Daron Acemoglu and Simon Johnson, Power and Progress: Our Thousand-Year Struggle Over Technology and Prosperity, Rajawat said while technology eventually adds jobs, it does so with a lag.

The people who lose work, he argued, are rarely the ones who gain from the new roles being created. While someone in their twenties may adapt to the shift, an employee in their forties or fifties is unlikely to do so, he added.

Trends reshaping the economy

Rajawat identified three trends reshaping the economy.

The old formula, wherein Rs 100 crore of investment generates around 10,000 jobs, no longer holds, he said. Plants manufacturing mobile phone and electric vehicles are heavily automated, and schemes such as the production-linked incentive are tied to capital rather than employment.

The second trend is the impact of AI and automation. AI is already affecting white-collar work across sectors. MSMEs, which he called the country's largest job engine, are also losing jobs to automation.

The third, which, he said, gets too little attention, is platform consolidation.

Rajawat argued that dominant ecommerce and social media platforms hold consumer data, which new entrepreneurs need, and this kind of monopoly prevents new businesses from succeeding. If entrepreneurship stalls, so does job creation, he said.

What Hundred Million Jobs is doing

Hundred Million Jobs works on ground projects, research, and advocacy across the country.

A consortium of six companies is helping the Rajasthan government turn its skilling mission into a jobs mission, on the premise that skilling is an input and jobs are the output that matters. In Kolhapur, the non-profit body is working with foundry and die-casting units to cut energy costs by shifting to renewables so that firms can compete, export and hire.

On the legal front, Hundred Million Jobs has formed a working group with sitting and former high court and Supreme Court judges. It is also planning a pilot with a high court to clear case backlog in a particular district using technology. Rajawat said slow enforcement of contracts and patents leaves solo entrepreneurs defenceless against large clients who do not pay.

The initiative is also lobbying for changes to data-ownership laws and for MSMEs to receive the same recognition as tech startups in entrepreneurship awards.

Rajawat also said Hundred Million Jobs has urged the skilling ministry to recognise displaced workers as a category needing support. And he wants the market, not the state, to provide support.

"Some of you should set up a company which does reskilling of displaced workers," he told the audience, calling it both a business opportunity and a way to create jobs.

A special thank you to Rawbare, our gifting partner, for adding a thoughtful touch to the TechSparks 2026 experience and making this year's edition even more memorable.

item.title: Rotoris bags Rs 70 Cr to expand its luxury watch business
item.description: The company plans to use the funds for research and development, expanded production, and growing its Rotoris House, its appointment-based space for meeting clients, presence in India and overseas.
item.content:encoded:
Gurugram-based independent luxury watchmaker Rotoris has raised Rs 70 crore (~$8.5 million) in a Series A funding round led by early-stage investment firm Blume Ventures.

9Unicorns and Centricity also participated, bringing in family-office investors including Diwakar Goel, BlackRock’s global head of data, former Coca-Cola Asia-Pacific group president Atul Singh and Adhiraj Burman of the Dabur family. Actor and television host Rannvijay Singha also invested.

The company plans to use the funds for research and development, expanded production, and growing its Rotoris House, its appointment-based space for meeting clients, presence in India and overseas.

The Gurugram-based watchmaker claims its first collection of 2,100 numbered timepieces sold out within days of its February 2026 launch. It asserted that nearly 1,00,000 people have since registered for access, while 40% of demand comes from outside India, including the US, Dubai, and Australia.

Blume Ventures sees an opportunity to build an Indian luxury brand with international ambitions. “We are backing their vision to make an Indian brand shine amongst global icons, and the timing has never been better,” said Karthik Reddy, co-founder and managing partner of Blume Ventures.

Rotoris produces limited-run analogue watches, releasing collections as named chapters with published production numbers. Its Manifesta collection features natural-stone dials, including lapis lazuli and imperial jade, making each dial distinct.

Astonia is a 42mm chronograph, a watch with a stopwatch function, made using steel, titanium and carbon and powered by a Swiss movement. Each timepiece is assembled and tested by hand at the company’s Gurugram Atelier, with movements sourced from Switzerland or Japan depending on the collection.

“The design creates the desire, but the engineering, assembly and attention to detail earn the trust,” co-founder Prerna Gupta said.

Co-founder Aakash Anand described a Rotoris watch as “a symbol of ambition, worn on the wrist”. He said the company plans to open Rotoris House in New York because many of its customers live there.

The expansion comes as Indian consumers increasingly trade up to higher-priced watches. Luxury and high-end watches accounted for 70% of sales in FY25, up from 48% in FY20. Younger buyers are showing greater interest in mechanical watches, distinctive designs and limited editions.

Trade policy could also reshape competition. The India-EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement, which took effect in October 2025, is expected to reduce import duties on qualifying watches from member countries, including Switzerland, over time. This could support greater access for international brands while raising competitive pressure on domestic manufacturers.

Other Indian watchmakers are pursuing international growth. In September, Bangalore Watch Company raised $1.4 million from its own customers, including family-office principals and high-net-worth individuals. Rotoris had previously raised $3 million in seed funding in December 2025.

item.title: Live2.ai raises Rs 130 Cr to expand its AI-led social commerce platform
item.description: The pre-Series B round, led by VC firm IvyCap Ventures, comprises fresh capital for business expansion and a secondary component for partial liquidity to early shareholders.
item.content:encoded:
Bengaluru-based Live2.ai, which uses artificial intelligence (AI) to connect social-media intelligence with marketing and commerce, has raised Rs 130 crore ($14 million) in a pre-Series B funding round led by venture capital firm IvyCap Ventures. 

The round combines fresh capital for business expansion and a secondary component that provides partial liquidity to early shareholders.

Live2.ai plans to invest the capital in its AI agent platform, expand enterprise deployments, strengthen cloud infrastructure across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific, and recruit engineers, data scientists, and customer success staff.

“Brands today are drowning in signals and starved of action,” said J Venkat, Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer, Live2.ai. The funding, he added, would help bring detection, decision-making, and activation into a single governed workflow for global enterprise customers.

The platform monitors conversations across Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Reddit, X, and review websites. It integrates trend analysis, influencer-content audits, campaign publishing, and performance measurement. It also converts content cleared for commercial use into shoppable experiences across websites, retail outlets, customer relationship management systems, and online marketplaces.

The investment reflects a wider shift in how brands use social media to understand consumer behaviour and drive sales. 

“Social has become a key channel for how consumers discover, evaluate, and buy, yet brands still rely on fragmented and manual tools to understand and act on it,” said Vikram Gupta, Founder and Managing Partner of IvyCap Ventures. He said Live2.ai was building an AI-native operating system to turn real-time cultural signals into commerce, with the security and governance required by global brands.

Co-founder and Chief Operating Officer Neha Suyal said the challenge is to turn intelligence into timely, measurable action at scale.

Live2.ai says it serves more than 200 brands across the United States, Europe and Southeast Asia, including Henkel’s Schwarzkopf, Titan Brands, and Shiseido. Revenue grew fourfold over the past 12 months, according to the company, with 90% generated outside India. 

The investment comes at a time when funding into Indian AI businesses is growing. Recent rounds include voice-AI startup Navana.ai’s Rs 40 crore Series A fundraise in September and enterprise software company Kapture’s $10 million pre-Series B funding in June.

Policy is evolving alongside the industry. The government’s IndiaAI Mission has an outlay of Rs 10,371.92 crore over five years to develop computing infrastructure, support domestic AI capabilities, and promote responsible adoption.

Governance guidelines issued in February this year propose national institutions for AI policy coordination and safety. Separately, consumer-affairs guidance requires clear disclosure of paid or barter influencer endorsements.

Edited by Swetha Kannan

item.title: AI startup Simplismart raises $14M from Dallas Venture Capital, Nvidia, and others
item.description: Simplismart said it will use the funding to develop its tech platform, for market expansion, and partnerships.
item.content:encoded:
AI inference infrastructure startup Simplismart has raised $14 million in a Series B funding round led by Dallas Venture Capital, with participation from NVIDIA, Accel, Shastra VC and Micromax.

The company will use the funds to further develop its AI inference platform, expand its partnerships with cloud providers and sovereign AI initiatives, and strengthen its presence in North America and other global markets.

Simplismart builds software that connects AI models with GPU infrastructure. Its modular inference engine enables businesses to configure models based on their speed, cost and performance requirements, while its orchestration platform manages deployment and scaling across cloud and on-premises infrastructure.

“We have spent four years building the software layer between the model and the GPU, helping customers optimise how their workloads are deployed and operated. This funding will allow us to take that platform to more enterprises and cloud providers globally,” said Amritanshu Jain, Co-founder and CEO, Simplismart.

The company said its annualised revenue run rate has grown 14-fold over the past six months. It counts companies such as HeyGen, Higgsfield, InVideo, Shiprocket, Apna and Ema among its customers, which use its platform to run production workloads across video, voice, multimodal and enterprise AI applications.

For its cloud-provider offering, Simplismart works with NVIDIA to deploy AI infrastructure. Unlike inference providers that purchase or reserve GPU capacity and resell it, Simplismart does not own compute infrastructure. Instead, it provides the software layer that enables third-party GPU fleets to run production AI workloads, positioning itself as a data centre enabler.

The platform allows cloud providers to offer managed AI services under their own brands without having to build the underlying software stack from scratch.

“Simplismart is rapidly emerging as a global player helping enterprises run AI workloads more efficiently, while enabling cloud providers to turn GPU capacity into scalable services. We are backing this fast-growing company because of its proven technical prowess in addressing a critical need in the AI infrastructure ecosystem globally, as well as the strong execution capabilities of its founding team,” said Dayakar Puskoor, Managing Partner, Dallas Venture Capital.

item.title: Matiks raises $10M in pre-Series A round led by General Catalyst
item.description: The company said it will use the funding to expand internationally, develop new games and social experiences, and launch an artificial intelligence (AI)-powered game creation platform that will enable users to build and publish games without writing code.
item.content:encoded:
Bengaluru-based social gaming platform Matiks has raised $10 million in a pre-Series A funding round led by General Catalyst. The round also saw participation from entrepreneur Ronnie Screwvala and existing investors Info Edge Ventures, Tanglin Venture Partners, and Untitled Ventures.

According to a statement by the company, the fresh capital will be used to expand internationally, develop new games and social experiences, and launch an artificial intelligence (AI)-powered game creation platform that will enable users to build and publish games without writing code.

Founded in 2024, Matiks develops games centred on mathematics, memory, logic and puzzles, combining competitive gameplay with social features.

In September 2026, 2.2 million people played 48 million games on the platform. Its daily active users have more than doubled since June to over 300,000, with early engagement emerging in markets including Japan, the US and South Korea, the compamy said.

“Over the last decade, we have made it incredibly easy to consume content but have done far less to make using our brains equally entertaining. We started Matiks with a simple belief: using your brain can be just as fun and addictive as any other form of entertainment," said Sudhanshu Bhatia, co-founder and chief executive officer of Matiks.

"Our ambition is to make mind sports as culturally relevant as physical sports and esports - giving mental athletes, puzzlers, and competitive players the visibility, communities, and recognition they deserve. With AI, we want anyone, anywhere in the world, to create a brain game that millions can play. We are not trying to get people off their phones; we are trying to give them something better to do on them,” he added.

The company said users who complete a seven-day streak show 62% retention one month later, while some early cohorts have retained 32% of users at week 52. Its recently launched single-player puzzle format, SNAC, has also driven longer engagement, with sessions that include the format running approximately three times longer.

Rahul Humayan, partner at General Catalyst, said the platform was addressing demand for alternatives to conventional digital content.

"Negative content is consuming a growing share of our screen time, and Matiks is building the alternative: a social platform for brain games where people challenge friends, learn from one another and, soon, use AI to create games of their own. Sudhanshu, Sushant and Mohan have built one of the most engaged communities we have seen in consumer, from everyday players to world champions, and they are now taking it global. We are proud to partner with them as they make brain games a category of their own," he said.

Matiks will initially prioritise expansion in the US before entering other tier-one markets. It also plans to increase investments in engineering, AI, product, design, game development and growth, alongside scaling creator partnerships and global distribution.

The company plans to develop an AI-powered game creation engine that will allow users to create, publish and share brain games across multiple formats. It expects user-generated content to increase the variety of games available on the platform.

item.title: Healthy snack brand Troovy raises Rs 100 Cr in Series B round led by Fireside Ventures
item.description: Gurugram-based Troovy will use the funding for R&D, expanding its manufacturing capacity, and scaling distribution across quick commerce and offline channels.
item.content:encoded:
Troovy, a food and snacks brand, has raised Rs 100 crore in a Series B round of funding led by Fireside Ventures, with participation from Sharrp Ventures and other investors.

The Gurugram-based brand will use the funding for R&D, expanding its manufacturing capacity, and scaling distribution across quick commerce and offline channels, as it looks to launch a wide range of products.

Troovy was founded in 2023 by Mansi Baranwal and Aditya Mukherjee with the goal of providing nutritious food. Its portfolio spans categories such as snacks, sauces and spreads, and millet pasta. It says its vacuum-cooked potato chips have 10-12% oil and high protein, compared with 35-40% oil in mainstream chips. It also promises clean-label ketchups and seasonings without synthetic additives or preservatives.

Troovy's co-founder & CBO Aditya Mukherjee said, "This backing (investment) is a vote of confidence in a model most food companies don't use: building with the people who'll actually eat what you make. When you build with users, you have to push innovation, because users don't settle. It's not enough to replace the oil and sugar; you have to reduce them dramatically.”

Troovy says it has engaged with over 100 mothers and their children through community-led discussions, recipe brainstorming, and product tastings. These conversations have helped shape the brand’s approach to creating snacks with good ingredients, without harmful preservatives or additives, while maintaining the taste that children expect, the company said.

Ankita Balotia, Principal, Fireside Ventures, said, "Troovy grew 5x in the eight months following our last investment, and that is what made us double down. The team has executed incredibly well on growth, and the backend supply chain.”

Troovy had raised $5 million in a Series A round of funding in January this year.
